> I don't think this would fix the issue. We don't know whether ACR is anonymous or not.
> 
> @awesomenix Have you checked with ACR team for supporting empty auth context?

`empty auth context` is we provide empty username and password, and thus we could access the anonymous ACR repo, that's guaranteed by ACR team, they came out the solution when I made the fix last time.

For MSI case, if we don't provide empty username and password(this PR removes the code for MSI), kubelet will only use MSI to communicate with ACR repo, so if that's an anonymous ACR repo, this will not work. 
add @sivagms @yuwaMSFT2 for any comments. Thanks.

issue_context.title: Unable to download from anonymous Azure Container Registry with containerd
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:

Problem is that
 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bfd8610ddafb2fcb2cb330187c8248777ea0b022/pkg/credentialprovider/azure/azure_credentials.go#L209
 
Seems like an empty username and password for AuthConfig is update for *azurecr* instead do not have an entry to keep a nil auth context.
 
But according to the code https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bfd8610ddafb2fcb2cb330187c8248777ea0b022/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_image.go#L44 this sends an empty AuthConfig since we update the structure with empty creds, which containerd doesn’t like
 
So instead of sending this
 
`imageRef, err := m.imageService.PullImage(imgSpec, nil, podSandboxConfig)`
 
 
we end up sending this
 
`imageRef, err := m.imageService.PullImage(imgSpec, auth, podSandboxConfig)`
 
with an empty auth context.
 
https://github.com/containerd/cri/blob/6dc2a874470f7489217a7c757da258356b92bfdb/pkg/server/image_pull.go#L190
 
which matches this error
 
```
Aug 27 16:39:37 containerd[4953]: time="2019-08-27T16:39:37.609386516Z" level=error msg="PullImage "repos.azurecr.io/mirror/download-amd64:v1" failed" error="failed to resolve image "repos.azurecr.io/mirror/download-amd64:v1": no available registry endpoint: invalid auth config"
```
 
**What you expected to happen**:

Containerd should successfully download from anonymous ACR

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

use kubelet to download pod from anonymous ACR with containerd CRI

**Anything else we need to know?**:

ideally the check should be made if the repo is anonymous, do not add to the config, which is done in MSI case. Worst case atleast add this to Service Principal case, but that would still be a hack
 
``` golang
else {
               // Add our entry for each of the supported container registry URLs
               for _, url := range containerRegistryUrls {
                       cred := &credentialprovider.DockerConfigEntry{
                               Username: a.config.AADClientID,
                               Password: a.config.AADClientSecret,
                               Email:    dummyRegistryEmail,
                       }
                       cfg[url] = *cred
               }
               // add ACR anonymous repo support: use empty username and password for anonymous access
                cfg["*.azurecr.*"] = credentialprovider.DockerConfigEntry{
                        Username: "",
                       Password: "",
                       Email:    dummyRegistryEmail,
                }
 
        }
 ```
 
 **Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.14.6
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): ubuntu
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments:
Since @awesomenix has present a pr for this issue.
/assign @awesomenix

There are multiple settings affected this

1. Deployment had an emptycredentials for imagepullsecrets, disabling it fixed the problem
2. Above may break in older kubernetes clusters for ACR + SP/ ACR + MSI, which is fixed with containerd >1.2.9

The issue was related to ACR + containerd, removing empty credentials from imagepull secrets solved the problem here. For older kubernetes cluster might want to upgrade containerd version

review_comments:
why remove this? when user use `UseManagedIdentityExtension`,  also needs to support ACR anonymous.
Original code will always have `empty username and password for anonymous access`, will that solve your issue?

When use uses `UseManagedIdentityExtension` we already check the authentication against the ACR, so if it supports anonymous, i think we do not add the credentials in the configuration, but if it does not support anonymous, the credentials are added for repo isnt it?

The original fix made was for service principal. Ideally we need to do the same as we do for MSI case and not add the service principal client id and secret if the repo is anonymous. 

I have complete explanation in the issue for the reason of this removal.
The provided credential may not be authz to the ACR, so empty auth context is required for both MSI and SPN.

Problem is that
 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bfd8610ddafb2fcb2cb330187c8248777ea0b022/pkg/credentialprovider/azure/azure_credentials.go#L209
 
Seems like an empty username and password for AuthConfig is update for *azurecr* instead do not have an entry to keep a nil auth context.
 
But according to the code https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bfd8610ddafb2fcb2cb330187c8248777ea0b022/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_image.go#L44 this sends an empty AuthConfig since we update the structure with empty creds, which containerd doesn’t like
 
So instead of sending this
 
`imageRef, err := m.imageService.PullImage(imgSpec, nil, podSandboxConfig)`
 
 
we end up sending this
 
`imageRef, err := m.imageService.PullImage(imgSpec, auth, podSandboxConfig)`
 
with an empty auth context.
 
https://github.com/containerd/cri/blob/6dc2a874470f7489217a7c757da258356b92bfdb/pkg/server/image_pull.go#L190
 
which matches this error
 
```
Aug 27 16:39:37 containerd[4953]: time="2019-08-27T16:39:37.609386516Z" level=error msg="PullImage "repos.azurecr.io/mirror/download-amd64:v1" failed" error="failed to resolve image "repos.azurecr.io/mirror/download-amd64:v1": no available registry endpoint: invalid auth config"
```
 
We need to specify a nil AuthConfig rather than an empty one
